clue.text: Bribe accompanying what could be a camel

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or buy off, a small bribe
accompanying someone is going with them

explanation.surface: Someone offers a backhander alongside a camel being traded.
explanation.walkthrough: The Camel was a First World War biplane built by the Sopwith company, so 'what could be a camel' points at the maker, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sopwith Camel was a famous British fighter aircraft, so a camel could be one built by that firm.

clue.text: Difficult situations when the East enters conflicts

indicators.note: the East goes inside the conflicts

parts.note: scraps are fights or squabbles
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Trouble arises when an Eastern power joins the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in scrapes is to be in awkward or troublesome predicaments.

clue.text: Leap like a star over the heavens

indicators.note: in a down clue the star sits above the heavens

parts.note: the Pole Star, Polaris
the sky is called the vault of heaven

explanation.surface: Jumping like a celestial body across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole vault is an athletics jump using a long flexible pole.

clue.text: Expression of one not very clear about love

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the unclear word goes around love

parts.note: dim means faint or indistinct
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A remark from someone vague on the subject of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set phrase or turn of speech.

clue.text: Concealing the punishment

explanation.surface: Hiding the evidence of a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding is both keeping out of sight and a slang term for a thrashing.

clue.text: Medical term which provides me with a boring article

parts.note: boring means dull
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of jargon from medicine supplies the speaker with a tedious piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Medulla is an anatomical word, as in medulla oblongata, the lower part of the brainstem.

clue.text: Where a minor is returned and without a majority

indicators.note: the majority goes outside, around the other piece

parts.note: many means a large number, most

indicators.note: the words a minor, read as a lad, run backwards

parts.note: a minor is a young person, a lad

explanation.surface: A place where a young person is sent back, lacking most of the votes.
explanation.walkthrough: MANDALAY is a city in Myanmar (Burma), famous from Kipling's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for a place, and Mandalay is a Burmese city.

clue.text: Presentable and so put on a piece of furniture

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Something fit to be shown once it has been placed on the dining furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatable means able to be given as a gift, presented to someone.

clue.text: It sounds like a failure for the northerners

indicators.note: the clue says the word for failure is said and heard as the answer

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or failure

explanation.surface: Something about the people of the north seems to signal a shortcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lapps, or Sami, live in the far north of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Is a name written incorrectly because of this ailment?

indicators.note: a name spelt wrongly has its letters out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether misspelling a name is a sign of a memory problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is a medical condition involving loss of memory.

clue.text: Right friendly when roused

parts.note: allied nations are on friendly terms

explanation.surface: A right-wing group turns sympathetic once stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops that are rallied are stirred up and gathered again for action.

clue.text: There is a certain amount of money in something to be aimed at

parts.note: nine pence, written 9p, is a definite sum of money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum of cash is lodged inside a target.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'certain amount' is literal: nine pence, NINE P.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninepin is one of the skittles a bowler tries to knock down.

clue.text: Everyone looks down on their pictures

definitions.text: Everyone looks down on their pictures

parts.words: Everyone looks down on their pictures
parts.note: sounds like contempt for some painters, but people literally look down at chalk drawings done on the ground of a street

explanation.definitionFit: Street painters draw in chalk on the paving, so passers-by gaze downwards at their work.

clue.text: Searched for with a sigh before the train starts

indicators.note: the sighing word comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: a sough is a murmuring or sighing sound, as of wind

indicators.note: the start of the word train is its first letter only

explanation.surface: Someone hunted, sighing, just before the train pulled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sought is the past tense of seek, to look for something.

clue.text: Composer who makes a countryman give out over an hour

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit above the hour

parts.note: a hind is a farm worker, a rustic
to emit is to give out
H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A musician who makes a farmhand produce something for an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Hindemith was a twentieth-century German composer.

clue.text: Where to spoil a girl

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
Bella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A question about where one might go to pamper a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: MARBELLA is a resort on Spain's Costa del Sol.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue asks for a place, and Marbella is a Spanish holiday town.

clue.text: If broken the glass might make the leg rotten

indicators.note: the words would be broken up and remade, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that a smashed glass could leave someone's leg in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in reverse: 'If broken', the answer's letters make 'leg rotten'; 'might make' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held to the eyes by a handle.

clue.text: Those who form queues for dishes

definitions.meaning: a queue is also a pigtail, and to plat is to plait

explanation.surface: People lining up for the food.
explanation.definitionFit: Platters are flat serving plates, and also people who braid pigtails, old sense of queue.

clue.text: Parking confuses means of propulsion

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: A car park layout bewilders the propulsion system.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddles are oars used to drive a canoe through water.

clue.text: Bachelor's button

parts.note: reads like a fastening on an unmarried man's shirt, but is a popular name for a yellow-flowered garden shrub

explanation.definitionFit: Kerria japonica, a shrub with pompom-like yellow flowers, is commonly called bachelor's buttons.

clue.text: Cared terribly about me being fined

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around me
done terribly means badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone was very upset to be penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cared terribly' is surface distress; 'terribly' shuffles the five letters, and 'about' wraps that jumble round the speaker. 'being' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is an old legal term for punishing with a monetary penalty.

clue.text: Make a great outcry or show politeness about a measure

indicators.note: the politeness word goes round the measure

parts.note: to bow is a courteous gesture
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Shout loudly, or be courteous about a quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to roar or shout loudly.

clue.text: Give assiduous service where the PM lives between social engagements

indicators.note: the prime minister's address sits in the middle of the two parties

parts.note: a dance is a social event
the plural gives a second dance
the British prime minister lives at 10 Downing Street, so at Ten

explanation.surface: Serve attentively at Downing Street between rounds of parties.
explanation.walkthrough: AT TEN is where the Prime Minister lives: Number 10 Downing Street, London.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance attendance on someone is an idiom for waiting on them eagerly and obsequiously.

clue.text: One chap turns up without love for a woman

indicators.note: the chap goes outside love
in a down clue the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a chap is a man
O is love, a nil score in tennis
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone man shows up having lost his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' puts MAN around O, giving MOAN; 'turns up' reverses I MOAN to give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, borne by Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible.

clue.text: If he lost heart, the fool would become a leader

definitions.text: If he lost heart, the fool would become a leader

parts.words: If he lost heart, the fool would become a leader
parts.note: the fool's word with its central letter removed leaves the Italian title of Mussolini, Il Duce

explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow learner, a fool, and Duce was the Italian dictator's title.

clue.text: Treat as a celebrity when tragic hero lives among the French

indicators.note: the hero and lives are placed inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
Ion is the title hero of a tragedy by Euripides
lives in the sense exists, is

explanation.surface: A tragic hero living in France is fêted.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise is to make much of someone as a celebrity.

clue.text: In a cult there is potential for going mad

indicators.note: the words could go into another arrangement, so their letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Joining a cult carries the risk of losing your mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic act is a crazy, insane one.

clue.text: Views about the left, which are insults

indicators.note: the views are wrapped around the left

parts.note: sights are views, things seen
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Opinions on the political left that are offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Slights are snubs, acts that belittle someone.

clue.text: Leisure time when knowledge is put into a gardening problem

indicators.note: the knowledge is placed inside the gardening problem

parts.note: a weed is an unwanted plant a gardener must deal with
ken means range of knowledge, as in beyond one's ken

explanation.surface: Spare time spent learning about a nuisance in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday and Sunday are the days off work for most people.
